beats.text: Same four hundred dollars of donations. Split across two returns, you get fifty-eight dollars back. Put them on one: eighty-seven.
Alex and Sam each gave two hundred dollars to charity in twenty twenty-five. Each claimed their own receipt.
The federal rule: the first two hundred dollars on a return gets fourteen and a half percent. Above that: twenty-nine.
Split, neither return gets past the first two hundred. Twenty-nine dollars each. Fifty-eight total.
Pooled on one return, the second two hundred jumps to twenty-nine percent. Twenty-nine more, same gifts.
The twist: you don't have to claim this year. Receipts can wait up to five years and stack. But the credit only cuts tax owed.
So pool them on the spouse who owes tax, before you file.
Next: moving for work or school, and the forty kilometre rule. Follow so you don't miss it.
